children: Japanese rubber futures fell on Tuesday, tracking a sharp drop in oil prices and weaker Tokyo equities, though losses were limited by falling inventories in top consumer China.
The Osaka Exchange rubber contract for April delivery
was down 4.6 yen, or 1.04%, at 437.3 yen ($2.74) per kg as of 0130 GMT
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange for January delivery
fell 310 yuan, or 1.58%, to 19,345 yuan ($2,902.82) per metric ton
The most active January butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) slid 605 yuan, or 3.74%, to 15,580 yuan per metric ton
fell 1.3% shortly after the open on Tuesday, as technology shares slid after the United States stepped up efforts to curb China's access to advanced AI chips
Weaker risk sentiment tends to weigh on rubber futures

Oil prices fell on Tuesday after settling more than 3% lower on Monday, as expectations of a supply surplus, fuelled by recovering Middle East exports, overshadowed concerns about continued attacks on tankers in the region
Natural rubber often takes direction from oil prices as it competes for market share with synthetic rubber, which is made from crude oil
However, a smaller-than-expected accumulation in Chinese inventories limited losses
Overseas supply is expected to increase, but domestic inventories are still falling, which limits downside for prices, analysts from broker GF Futures said in a note
Rubber inventories in warehouses monitored by the Shanghai Futures Exchange fell 3.1% week-on-week, the exchange said on Friday
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for February delivery (STFG7) last traded at 246.9 US cents per kg, down 1.1%
